title: Research

Latest working paper

Sustaining the Unsustainable? Greek Government Debt Before and After the Euro
Job market paper · Working paper · [Month Year] · PDF


Abstract

Using hand-collected fiscal data for 1957–2008, I ask how Greece sustained a high and apparently unsustainable level of government debt for decades, even though conventional empirical sustainability criteria point to unsustainability since at least the 1970s. I argue that the institutional transition into the euro area explains the timing. Before the euro, inflation, monetary accommodation, and currency depreciation relaxed the effective financing constraint and postponed the crisis. Euro membership removed these mechanisms. title: Teaching
text: I teach economics to undergraduate and MBA students, both in person and online. Each course is organized around a small number of central questions.

title: Teaching
text:
Principles of Microeconomics
Undergraduate · in person and online

Central question: how is price determined?
The course uses the supply and demand model to explain how prices are set, then asks how the model changes under different market structures:

Perfect competition
Monopoly
Oligopoly
Monopolistic competition

title: Teaching
text:
Principles of Macroeconomics
Undergraduate · in person and online

Central questions: how can an economy achieve long-run growth, and how can we reduce short-run fluctuations?

Macroeconomic indicators: how we measure output, prices, and unemployment.
The long run: the determinants of economic growth.
Money, banking, and the Federal Reserve: how money is created and how monetary policy works.
The short run: why the economy fluctuates, and what policy can do about it.
